title: Rumi: The Beloved Is Right Here
subtitle: Eight Persian Sufi poems with English translation
yt_title: Rumi: The Beloved Is Right Here | 8 Persian Sufi Poems (English Translation)
intro: We often look for meaning far away: in other cities, other people, long journeys.
Rumi keeps turning us around, toward what is already close.
Here are eight passages about the Beloved who is nearer than we think.

poems.name: O People Gone on Pilgrimage

lines.fa: ای قوم به حج رفته کجایید کجایید
lines.en: O people gone on pilgrimage, where are you, where are you?

lines.fa: معشوق همین جاست بیایید بیایید
lines.en: The Beloved is right here. Come, come.

lines.fa: معشوق تو همسایه و دیوار به دیوار
lines.en: Your Beloved is your neighbour, wall to wall;

lines.fa: در بادیه سرگشته شما در چه هوایید
lines.en: wandering lost in the desert, what are you longing for?

tafsir: Rumi is not mocking the pilgrimage.
He is asking what the pilgrims are really looking for.
The Beloved lives next door, he says. Wall to wall.
The longest journey may be the one we take to avoid looking close by.

poems.name: The Veil Is You

lines.fa: ده بار از آن راه بدان خانه برفتید
lines.en: Ten times you took that road to that house;

lines.fa: یک بار از این خانه بر این بام برآیید
lines.en: just once, climb from this house up onto this roof.

lines.fa: با این همه آن رنج شما گنج شما باد
lines.en: Still, may all your hardship become your treasure;

lines.fa: افسوس که بر گنج شما پرده شمایید
lines.en: what a pity that the veil over your treasure is you.

tafsir: The same ghazal continues, with great tenderness.
Rumi blesses the pilgrims: may your hardship turn into treasure.
And then the gentle sting: the only thing hiding your treasure is you.
Climb onto your own roof, he says. Look up from where you already are.

poems.name: Open the Door

lines.fa: هین که منم بر در در برگشا
lines.en: Listen, it is I at the door: open the door.

lines.fa: بستن در نیست نشان رضا
lines.en: A closed door is no sign of welcome.

lines.fa: در دل هر ذره تو را درگهیست
lines.en: In the heart of every speck of dust there is a doorway for you;

lines.fa: تا نگشایی بود آن در خفا
lines.en: until you open it, that door stays hidden.

tafsir: Who is knocking here? The Beloved, at the door of our heart.
And the doors are everywhere: one in every speck of dust.
The Beloved is not hard to find. The doors are simply closed.
Our part is small and simple: open.

poems.name: Where Is Your Home?

lines.fa: ایا سر کرده از جانم تو را خانه کجا باشد
lines.en: O you who rose out of my soul, where is your home?

lines.fa: الا ای ماه تابانم تو را خانه کجا باشد
lines.en: O my shining moon, where is your home?

lines.fa: تو گویی خانهٔ خاقان بود دل‌های مشتاقان
lines.en: You say the hearts of longing lovers are the emperor's house;

lines.fa: مرا دل نیست ای جانم تو را خانه کجا باشد
lines.en: but I have no heart left, my soul: so where is your home?

tafsir: Rumi plays a lovely game here.
The Beloved lives in lovers' hearts, they say.
But I have given my heart away, so where can you live?
The answer is hidden in the question: where the self has emptied, the Beloved moves in.

poems.name: I Travelled to Every City

lines.fa: سفر کردم به هر شهری دویدم
lines.en: I travelled, I ran to every city;

lines.fa: به لطف و حسن تو کس را ندیدم
lines.en: I saw no one with your grace and beauty.

lines.fa: ز هجران و غریبی بازگشتم
lines.en: I came back from separation and exile,

lines.fa: دگرباره بدین دولت رسیدم
lines.en: and reached this good fortune once more.

tafsir: This is the story of many lives.
We go out searching, city after city.
And the best thing we find is what we came back to.
Travel can teach us that home was precious all along.

poems.name: You Are the Cave

lines.fa: یار مرا غار مرا عشق جگرخوار مرا
lines.en: My friend, my cave, my heart-devouring love,

lines.fa: یار تویی غار تویی خواجه نگهدار مرا
lines.en: you are the friend, you are the cave: master, keep me safe.

lines.fa: دانه تویی دام تویی باده تویی جام تویی
lines.en: You are the seed and the snare, the wine and the cup;

lines.fa: پخته تویی خام تویی خام بمگذار مرا
lines.en: you are the ripe and the raw: do not leave me raw.

tafsir: The cave recalls the Prophet hiding in a cave with his closest friend.
For Rumi, the Beloved is both the friend and the shelter.
Then everything becomes the Beloved: the bait and the trap, the wine and the cup.
And one simple prayer: do not leave me unripe. Finish what you began in me.

poems.name: One Soul

lines.fa: هیچ کسی سیر شد ای پسر از جان خویش
lines.en: Has anyone ever grown tired of their own soul, young friend?

lines.fa: جان منی چون یکیست جان من و جان تو
lines.en: You are my soul, since my soul and yours are one.

tafsir: We never grow tired of being alive.
Rumi says the Beloved is like that for him.
Not someone outside. His own soul.
When love is real, the line between me and you grows very thin.

poems.name: Like This

lines.fa: هر کی ز حور پرسدت رخ بنما که همچنین
lines.en: Whoever asks you about the beauties of paradise, show your face: like this.

lines.fa: هر کی ز ماه گویدت بام برآ که همچنین
lines.en: Whoever speaks to you of the moon, go up on the roof: like this.

lines.fa: هر طرفی که بشنوی نالهٔ عاشقانه‌ای
lines.en: Wherever you hear a lover's lament,

lines.fa: قصهٔ ماست آن همه حق خدا که همچنین
lines.en: it is all our story, by God: like this.

tafsir: This is one of Rumi's most beloved ghazals, with its refrain: hamchonin, like this.
Do not describe the Beloved. Show it.
And every love song you hear anywhere in the world is our story too.
The Beloved is not far. Look around: like this.
